lesson.content:
## What it is
Multiplexing is a technique that lets several signals share one communication link. [p. 1]
## Real-life analogy
Imagine you have a single radio station broadcasting music, news, and sports. Instead of having separate stations for each type of content, one station can broadcast all these different types of content at once. [p. 1]
## How it works
1. **Combining signals**: A multiplexer (MUX) combines multiple signals into one stream of data. [p. 1]
2. **Separating signals**: A demultiplexer (DEMUX) separates the combined stream back into its original signals at the receiving end. [p. 1]
## Key terms
- **Multiplexer (MUX)**: A device that combines multiple signals into one. [p. 1]
- **Demultiplexer (DEMUX)**: A device that separates a combined signal back into its original signals. [p. 1]
## Example
Let's say we have three signals: a music signal, a news signal, and a sports signal. Using FDM, we can combine these signals into one stream. At the receiving end, the demultiplexer will separate the combined signal back into its original three signals. [p. 1]
## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 1]
## Exam tip
Be able to explain the difference between FDM and TDM, and how they are used in different scenarios. [p. 1]
